title: Local‐Site Minimally Invasive Soft Tissue Management (LMI‐STM): A New Concept Reshaping the Paradigm of Peri‐Implant Soft Tissue Augmentation
content: Adequate peri-implant soft tissue thickness and keratinized mucosa width are prerequisites for the long-term stability, esthetic outcome, and peri-implant health of implant-supported restorations. Conventional augmentation with palatal free gingival grafts or connective tissue grafts requires a second surgical site, and donor-site pain and discomfort are the principal reasons why patients decline the procedure. Local techniques - the roll flap, modified roll flap, VIP-CT flap, and locally harvested small-volume CTG - avoid distant harvesting but have been reported in isolation. This article proposes Local-site Minimally Invasive Soft Tissue Management (LMI-STM), in which donor harvesting is confined to the implant site and its adjacent regions. The concept is organized along two axes - flap blood supply and the phenotype component targeted - yielding three procedure types and one unoccupied quadrant. A three-step decision framework defines when a local approach is appropriate and when to convert to a distant graft or substitute. Controlled studies using standardized volumetric and patient-reported outcomes are now required.
